clue.text: Former Latin question disheartened mother

indicators.note: to dishearten a word here is to take out its heart, the four letters at the middle of this eight-letter word

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A Latin scholar's old enquiry has lost heart, and so has his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes ESTI, the middle four letters, out of QUESTION, leaving QUON.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is borrowed straight from Latin, where it means formerly or at one time, hence an English adjective for one-time.

clue.text: Cleric turns up in part of harbour, trembling

indicators.note: the reversed title goes inside the harbour word

parts.note: a quay is a landing place in a harbour

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means written upwards, backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a cleric

explanation.surface: A priest arrives at the docks, shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' sounds like arriving but reverses REV to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: A quavery voice is one that shakes or trembles.

clue.text: Leaving home is becoming unfashionable

explanation.surface: Someone moving out of the family house is falling out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means literally heading out the door, and figuratively declining in popularity.

clue.text: Wind blowing round Arabian port

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation
blowing suggests something scattered about by the wind, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A gale blows around a harbour town in Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as a gale in the surface; it is the anagram fodder, and 'blowing' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwin is the port capital of Australia's Northern Territory.

clue.text: Petrol put in a car taking bananas over island

indicators.note: in a down clue the word goes over, that is above, the rest

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, mad

indicators.note: the fuel is placed inside the two words a car

parts.note: petrol is gas in American English

explanation.surface: Someone fills a car with fuel before going crazy over an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' is not fruit but slang for crazy, MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is the large island off the south-east coast of Africa.

clue.text: One must take turns to pull in the ropes

definitions.text: One must take turns to pull in the ropes

parts.words: One must take turns to pull in the ropes
parts.note: reads like a sailor taking turns on a rota, but it describes a revolving drum on deck that winds in cable as it turns

explanation.surface: A crew member has to take a shift hauling in the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: This ship's winch is a vertical drum turned round and round to haul in heavy ropes and anchor cables.

clue.text: Patient demanding action

explanation.surface: An invalid insists on treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor speaks of a patient as a case, and a lawsuit is a case or legal action.

clue.text: One hopes to be engaged as member of debating team

explanation.surface: A debater wants to land a job.
explanation.walkthrough: A suitor makes a proposal of marriage; in a formal debate, the side moving the motion are its proposers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pops the question is a proposer, and in debating the team moving a motion are its proposers.

clue.text: Pull belly up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means written from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the gut is the belly

explanation.surface: Someone draws in their stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a sharp pull, and to tug is to pull hard.

clue.text: Puzzle having no place among students

indicators.note: among means the abbreviation goes inside the students' union

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain
pl is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A conundrum with no answer turns up on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: NUS is the British National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to puzzle or baffle them.

clue.text: A short distance behind

parts.note: a foot, abbreviated FT, is a short distance

explanation.surface: Someone trails just a little way back.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the word means towards the stern, that is, behind.

clue.text: To protect vehicle from attack, loaded eight rounds

indicators.note: loaded in the sense of drunk or packed in any old way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Guarding a coach against bandits, someone loads a gun with eight bullets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' looks like the gun being charged with eight rounds; it is the anagram signal on EIGHT ROUNDS.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from the Wild West guard who sat beside a stagecoach driver holding a shotgun to fend off robbers.

clue.text: Engine's velocity can be altered for certain periods of time

indicators.note: altering the letters means rearranging them into a new order

parts.note: v is the standard symbol for velocity in physics

explanation.surface: A mechanic notes that the speed of a motor can be adjusted at certain times.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenings are the recurring periods at the end of each day, so they are particular stretches of time.

clue.text: Official studies union law to begin with

parts.note: to con a text is to study it closely, so cons means studies

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words before it are taken

explanation.surface: A trade-union officer reads up on employment law first.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is a government official posted abroad to look after his country's citizens and trade.

clue.text: Coppers made little difference

explanation.surface: Police officers achieved very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police but means copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Small change is loose low-value coins such as copper pennies, and also something trivial or of little consequence.

clue.text: Better to enlist assistance for strike

indicators.note: enlisting takes the other word into its ranks, inside it

parts.note: a better, one who bets, is a backer
a hand is help, assistance

explanation.surface: A gambler recruits help for a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective but is one who bets, a BACKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhander is a blow struck with the back of the hand.

clue.text: The time is indeed right

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, indeed

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that the hour is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a fixed span of time, the period of one orbit of the sun.

clue.text: Vehicles, say, used in Wacky Races

indicators.note: the synonym is placed inside the jumbled letters
wacky means crazy, so the letters of the following word are jumbled

parts.note: to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: Cars of a family sort appear in a famous cartoon about a madcap motor rally.
explanation.walkthrough: Wacky Races is a cartoon series about a crazy car race; here 'Wacky' is the anagram signal, making ECARS, with 'used in' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate cars are what British drivers call station wagons, so they are a kind of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Reserve time in holiday area

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the holiday word

parts.note: the seaside is where Britons go on holiday

explanation.surface: Someone books some time at a holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside is to put something by in reserve for later use.

clue.text: Unite' to put taxi firms out of business?

definitions.text: to put taxi firms out of business?

explanation.surface: Rival cab companies band together, or perhaps shut up shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A taxi rank is a stand where cabs wait for fares; shutting the ranks would put cab firms out of business.
explanation.definitionFit: To close ranks is an idiom for a group drawing together to protect its members, and literally shutting cab stands.

clue.text: In America, one prizes Indian watering-hole

parts.note: the Crow are a Native American people
a bar is a watering-hole, a place to drink

explanation.surface: A Native American values his local saloon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prizes' means levers open; Americans spell it with a z where British write prise.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is an iron lever used to force or prise things open.

clue.text: Smart learner in school

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the word for school

parts.note: a gam is a school, or herd, of whales
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A clever pupil is enrolled at an academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' suggests a classroom but means a group of whales, a GAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Glam, short for glamorous, describes someone fashionably smart in appearance.

clue.text: Sailor's destiny, ,to be under naval officer

indicators.note: in a down clue being under means placed below, after the other word

parts.note: a mate is a ship's officer
one's lot is one's fate, destiny

explanation.surface: A seaman's fate is to serve below a superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor's' is read as 'sailor is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British slang, from French, for a sailor; the clue's apostrophe-s stands for is.

clue.text: Fine young man you once sheltered is flogged

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: sheltered means the old pronoun goes inside the word for boy

parts.note: a lad is a young man
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A good young man once protected you, and was whipped for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To flay is to whip so hard the skin comes off, so flayed means severely flogged.

clue.text: Money needed upfront to be top egg producer?

explanation.surface: Initial capital is required for whoever wants to lead in poultry farming.
explanation.walkthrough: Out- as a prefix means to beat at something (outrun, outsell), so to out-lay is to beat other hens at laying eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is a sum spent at the start of a venture, and in the whimsical sense to outdo rival hens at laying.

clue.text: Letters sent back to Irish lad about mum

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the name is written backwards

parts.note: Liam is a common Irish boy's name
mum, as in keep mum, means silence, so the hush sign sh

indicators.note: back means the little word that follows is written in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone returns correspondence to a young Irishman about his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses LIAM to MAIL and 'back' reverses TO to OT; 'mum' is silence, SH, not a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A mailshot is a batch of letters, often advertising, sent out to many people at once.

clue.text: Supporter missing beginning of driving competition

indicators.note: the opening letter of the competition word is lost

parts.note: a rally is a motoring competition

explanation.surface: A fan misses the start of a motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a friend who backs you, a supporter.

clue.text: Bach's first two pieces composed —- indeed — for a special occasion abroad

parts.note: the first two letters of the composer's name
composed means calmed, stilled
ay is an old form of yes, indeed

explanation.surface: Two of a composer's opening works were indeed written for a festive event in another country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' suggests music writing but means calmed, STILLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastille Day, 14 July, is France's national holiday, a celebration held abroad from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: So disgusting, when heard

indicators.note: when heard means spoken, so the word is what it sounds like

parts.note: sick, in slang, means disgusting

explanation.surface: Something is so revolting, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC is Latin for thus, printed in brackets to mean 'so written'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word means thus or so, used to show a quotation is reproduced exactly.

clue.text: Penniless, having nothing

explanation.surface: Someone with no money has nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil means zero; a person with nil in the bank has no funds, and nil is also a score of nothing.

clue.text: First removed pots in garden

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for pots is taken away

parts.note: crockery is pots, plates and cups collectively

explanation.surface: The plant pots were taken out of the garden first.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, the first letter of CROCKERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockery is a garden, or part of one, made of stones with alpine plants growing between them.

clue.text: Duke's head in freshly-minted coin

indicators.note: the initial goes inside the word for new

parts.note: something freshly minted is recent, new

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A nobleman's portrait appears on newly struck money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests the portrait on a coin but picks D from Duke's.
explanation.definitionFit: A red cent is an American cent piece of copper, a coin of tiny value.
